name: Clunes

facts.claim: Clunes is a town 36 km north of Ballarat in the Shire of Hepburn
Gold was first found in Victoria's first registered discovery here in 1850 and mining ran into the 1890s
The town is one of Victoria's most intact gold-rush towns and Australia's only International Booktown, with second-hand bookshops
Clunes Museum is in a c.1860 warehouse; entry by gold coin donation

access_note: Booktown festival is annual and is not a permanent attraction; keep out of bio
unresolved: Festival dates conflict between sources (not needed)

name: Blue Waters Lake

facts.claim: Blue Waters is a former open-cut mine now filled with water, in Creswick Regional Park near Creswick
About 800 m walk from the first parking area leads to the water
Parks Victoria lists it as a site of Creswick Regional Park, which is free to enter
The 14.5 km Creswick Waters Walk circuit passes Blue Waters, St Georges Lake and Cosgrove Reservoir

access_note: Access road potholed, 4WD needed further down in wet weather (goldfieldsguide)
unresolved: No explicit 'free' statement read on the Parks Victoria page

name: Ballarat to Skipton Rail Trail

facts.claim: The trail runs 53 km along the old Skipton railway line from western Ballarat through Haddon, Smythesdale and Pittong to Skipton
It was resurfaced after years in poor condition
Route map published by Golden Plains Shire

access_note: Placement wiki title 'Ballarat to Skipton Rail Trail' 404s; the article is 'Ballarat–Skipton Rail Trail' (en dash). Length: 53 km Wikipedia, other sources 55-63 km

name: Bendigo Art Gallery

facts.claim: One of Australia's oldest and largest regional art galleries, owned by the City of Greater Bendigo
Collection emphasises 19th century European art and Australian art from the 1800s, with contemporary Australian work
General admission is free; major touring exhibitions are ticketed separately

access_note: Ticketed exhibitions cost extra (e.g. one past show $35 adult) and are temporary; not the cost

name: Central Deborah Gold Mine

facts.claim: A non-active gold mine and tourist attraction in Bendigo, on the Victorian Heritage Register since 1999
929 kg of gold was extracted from the mine
The Mine Experience Tour goes 61 m underground and runs 75 minutes
Surface heritage buildings and a museum are open on a separate ticket, included with underground tours

access_note: Mine Experience Tour adult $40 (conc $35). Surface-only adult $8.50. Other prices on page ($29.50, $30, $65) are tram/bundle tours.

name: Golden Dragon Museum

facts.claim: Museum of Chinese Australian culture and history, on the site of one of Bendigo's old Chinatowns
The precinct includes Chinese Gardens and a Kuan Yin temple
Housed at 1-11 Bridge Street in the Dai Gum San precinct
First accredited museum in Victoria

access_note: Only price on home page is 'Group Bookings Adults: $15 | Concession: $12'; individual general admission price not shown. Older sources: $11 (2017), $16 (undated review).
unresolved: General admission adult price not found on official page; Tickets/Plan Your Visit subpages timed out or 404

name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Bendigo

facts.claim: Gothic Revival Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Sandhurst at 80 Wattle Street, Bendigo
Designed in 1895 by Reed, Barnes and Tappin; work resumed in 1954 and finished in 1977
Main spire is 87 m high, making it one of Australia's largest churches and the third tallest after Melbourne's two cathedrals
Building is 75 m long with a 24 m ceiling height and is on the Victorian Heritage Register

unresolved: No official cathedral page; free entry not stated by any source, assumed free (unverified)

facts.claim: About 60 acres of lawns, leafy trees, statues, a historic conservatory, a fernery and a playground on the edge of Bendigo's centre
On the corner of View Street and Pall Mall; open all hours
Site of the 1850s Government Camp, transformed from a goldfield into a public park
Has the Poppet Head Lookout Tower

name: Greater Bendigo National Park

facts.claim: 17,020-hectare national park created in 2002 from Whipstick State Park, Kamarooka State Park, One Tree Hill Regional Park and state forests
Protects Box-Ironbark forest, broombush mallee and grassy woodlands, with spring wildflowers and Swift Parrots
Old Tom Mine Walk passes gold-rush mine remains and fossicking is allowed
Flagstaff Hill Loop Walk and Big Hill Lookout give views over the Mallee and rural land; One Tree Hill has walking tracks and views over Bendigo

facts.claim: Artificial lake in Daylesford, formed when a dam wall was built across Wombat Creek in 1929
Designed by Walter Burley Griffin, the architect who won the competition to design Canberra
Lake submerged market gardens, mineral springs and the old Chinese settlement
Listed by visitor guide as a place to fish, among Daylesford's natural attractions
19th-century botanic gardens on Wombat Hill in Daylesford, on the Victorian Heritage Register
A picturesque setting for a walk or picnic, with a moist fern gully
Conifers and exotic trees show how European trees acclimatised to cold conditions at this altitude
Crown land with Hepburn Shire Council as committee of management; gardens celebrated 150 years in 2013

name: Hepburn Mineral Springs Reserve

facts.claim: 30-hectare reserve at Hepburn Springs with several mineral springs used for drinking and bathing since the 1860s
Part of Hepburn Regional Park and on the Victorian Heritage Register
Mineral spring pumps across the area are freely accessible for sipping the water
Hepburn Bathhouse & Spa reopened in September 2008 after a A$13 million redevelopment (paid spa, separate from the reserve)

unresolved: Bathhouse spa official site unreachable; spa price not recorded (extra inside the reserve, not the spot cost)

name: Convent Gallery

facts.claim: Former convent and boarding school of almost 90 years, on the crest of Wombat Hill overlooking Daylesford
Seven gallery spaces, museums, a chapel, gift shop and cafe over four levels, with gardens
Located in the Spa region of Daylesford, Central Victoria

access_note: Site lists Thursday to Monday opening only (hours not recorded)

name: Hepburn Regional Park

facts.claim: Regional park around Daylesford, Hepburn and Hepburn Springs with waterfalls, mineral springs and Gold Rush relics
Mineral springs include Sailors Falls, Tipperary, Golden and Argyle Springs; Jacksons Lookout tower gives panoramic views
Part of the 210 km Goldfields Track runs through it; The Blowhole shows 1850s gold-mining diversion of Sailors Creek
Jointly managed with the Dja Dja Wurrung

access_note: Parks Victoria reports storm damage: Twin Bridges to Tipperary Springs (east side) and Blowhole to Golden Spring tracks closed until further notice

name: Mineral Springs Loop Walk

facts.claim: Walk in Hepburn Regional Park giving a view of Sailors Falls
Passes mineral springs in the Hepburn Springs area

facts.claim: Spa town in the middle of the largest concentration of mineral springs in Australia, 48 km north-east of Ballarat
Visitors can sip mineral water from freely accessible spring pumps
Soak at the Hepburn Bathhouse and Spa
Plunges more than 32 m down a basalt cliff, the highest single drop of any waterfall in Central Victoria
Steps or a gently sloped path lead down from the car park to a lookout
In Coliban River Scenic Reserve near Trentham; strongest in winter and spring

name: Hanging Rock

facts.claim: Former volcano 718 m above sea level, 105 m above the plain, about 70 km north-west of Melbourne
Six-million-year-old volcanic formation with a sealed Summit Walking Trail; setting of Picnic at Hanging Rock
Reserve has a discovery centre and cafe
Dogs not permitted on the summit trail

access_note: Entry per vehicle (car $15, walk-in $5); closed to non-racegoers 1 and 26 Jan; summit trail closes in high wind and extreme fire danger

name: Mount Macedon Memorial Cross

facts.claim: A 21 m high First World War memorial cross of pale yellow terracotta tiles on a steel base, dedicated in 1935
Stands in a reserve near the summit of Mount Macedon, reached by a 4 km access road, and is visible from the plains below
Became a symbol of survival after the 1983 Ash Wednesday bushfires; an Anzac Day dawn service is held at its base

unresolved: No fee statement found; free open reserve assumed, unverified

facts.claim: A town in the Macedon Ranges, about 86 km from Melbourne, bypassed by the Calder Freeway
Piper Street has the oldest streetscape in town and still has many original buildings
Local points of interest include the Botanic Gardens and walks along the Campaspe River; farmers markets make it a day-trip town
A town of about 6,700 people in the Shire of Macedon Ranges, roughly halfway between Melbourne and Bendigo
Became a thoroughfare for gold-diggers heading through the Black Forest after gold was found in the 1850s
Close to Mount Macedon, Hanging Rock and several waterfalls, in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range

name: Kyneton Botanic Gardens

facts.claim: Botanic gardens on Mollison Street, Kyneton, established in 1858 and of state heritage significance
Features include bluestone garden walls, a wrought iron main gate, a rotunda, a fairy ring of trees and a 1902 drinking fountain
A riverside walk along the Campaspe River runs beside the gardens

unresolved: Wikipedia has no article (404); wiki null

name: Turpins Falls

facts.claim: An 18 m waterfall over basalt cliffs formed by an ancient lava flow on the Campaspe River, about 15 minutes north of Kyneton
A short, steep path of about 150 m from the car park, with a staircase, leads to a lookout; about 20 minutes return
Falls flow year-round, strongest after winter and spring rain, and may shrink to a trickle in summer
Reopened in April 2026 with a new viewing platform and staircase after about five years closed

facts.claim: A town in the Shire of Mount Alexander, 19 km from Castlemaine, kept largely as it was in the gold-rush days
Declared Australia's first notable town by the National Trust in 1966 for its 1850s buildings and mining heritage
Landmarks include the Beehive Chimney, Mount Tarrengower and its tower, and the Maldon railway station; one mine is open to the public
